instruction: Create and insert under 'Main Results' a summary table from '~/Documents/awesome-desktop/expe-results.xlsx' listing each model's name, OS score, Chrome score, and average score.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting specific columns (model, os, chrome, avg) from the Excel file and inserting as a table under 'Main Results' section in Word document. The evaluator verifies: (1) table has correct 4 column headers (25% weight), (2) at least 2 data rows with correct column count (15% weight), (3) table is located after 'Main Results' section heading (20% weight), and (4) table data matches the Excel source file with at least 2 cells matching per row (40% weight). This comprehensive check ensures both structural correctness and data accuracy from the source Excel file.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator comprehensively checks ALL instruction requirements: headers (model, os, chrome, avg), location after 'Main Results' section, and data correspondence with Excel source
Multi-getter architecture correctly extracts both Word document table and Excel source data for comparison
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' - directly accesses expected.get('table_index'), not expected.get('rules')
Data verification logic (40% weight) compares Word table content with Excel source, requiring at least 2 cells to match per row
Location verification logic tracks table position relative to 'Main Results' heading in document
Postconfig properly saves document with Ctrl+S to ensure fresh file state before verification
Weighted scoring is well-balanced: 25% headers, 15% row count, 20% location, 40% data match
Minor issue: Table position comparison logic (line 94-102 in getter) compares paragraph index with element index, which may cause incorrect location detection in some edge cases
Minor issue: Flexible matching requires only 50% cell match (2 out of 4 cells), which may be too lenient for some data verification scenarios
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Improve table position detection by using consistent index system (e.g., count all elements sequentially or use element relationships)
Consider increasing minimum cell match threshold from 2 to 3 cells for 4-column tables to ensure stricter data accuracy
Add string-to-number conversion for numeric columns (os, chrome, avg scores) before comparison to handle type differences
